record.tranche_reason: The post develops and evaluates a proposed detector for SAE feature absorption, but does not test the listed claims about superposition, polysemanticity, LLM feature geometry, or canonical SAE units.
record.gate_note: The theoretical absorption examples and lemmas are not empirical tests. The reported experiment evaluates whether a detector based on non-co-occurrence and similar downstream ablation effects identifies absorption; it does not establish that the listed claim versions hold. The author also reports a qualitative sanity check of the strongest causal links.
record.test_reason: The post proposes and evaluates a detector for SAE feature absorption in Gemma-2-2b SAEs. Its only empirical results are about the detector's (poor) performance and a qualitative sanity check of causal links between latents. It reports no rate or strength of superposition, polysemanticity, SAE feature recovery, canonicity or dimensionality. Absorption bears loosely on V5, since absorbed latents are not canonical units, but the post assumes absorption from prior work and measures no prevalence. So it tests none of the versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The author reports that the detector does not currently work. The metric is not bimodal and not strongly correlated with subjective absorption judgments. More data may fix coincidental matches but likely not the co-occurrence or single-token false positives.
record.recipe_differences: The post proposes a downstream-SAE ablation and effect-vector cosine detector for feature absorption, rather than testing the original toy-model superposition claim.
record.method_sensitivity: The post notes that the method can fail if the later SAE has the same absorption as the earlier SAE. It also describes candidate false positives from coincidental causal effects and from single-token latents; the proposed co-occurrence data is based on ~1e6 prompts.

fits_no_version.finding: In Gemma-2-2b (L20 MLP SAE to L21 residual SAE), cosine similarity of downstream ablation-effect vectors for non-co-occurring latent pairs was not bimodal. It was not strongly correlated with subjective judgments of absorption.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Shared downstream causal effect between non-co-occurring SAE latents does not reliably detect feature absorption.

fits_no_version.finding: The strongest causal links between L20 MLP SAE latents and L21 residual SAE latents mostly joined latents with plausibly related meanings.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Ablation-based causal links between adjacent-layer SAE latents are mostly semantically coherent.

record.problems: The detector evaluation is reported qualitatively without numerical correlation values or uncertainty estimates. Subjective judgments and examples are used to assess apparent absorption; the author notes possible coincidental matches and false positives that may persist despite more data.
record.rows_left_out: No additional empirical outcomes relevant to the claim versions were reported. The formal toy examples and lemmas are theoretical, not experimental results.

untested.parts: Toy-model storage geometry, sparsity-dependent transition and regular geometry; the post's formal model assumes orthonormal features.
Capacity competition as the cause of polysemanticity.
Distributed features in LLMs and SAE recovery of sparse features.
Completeness, stability and canonicity of SAE features. Absorption is assumed from prior work, and its prevalence is not measured.

record.verdict_notes: The theoretical lemmas on the subset and intersection cases are constructions, not empirical tests. The results are qualitative only, with no numbers reported. The post is not an original source for any version.

versions.untested_parts: Toy-model superposition, overlap geometry, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry are not tested.
The post does not test whether polysemantic neurons result from capacity competition or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
It does not test causes of polysemantic neurons apart from capacity pressure.
It does not measure whether LLM features are spread across neurons or whether SAEs recover sparse features.
The proposed detector is not a test of whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units.
The post's formal examples use vector-valued features, but it does not empirically test whether represented features are one-dimensional.

rows.subject: google/gemma-2-2b
rows.operation_detail: Ablate Layer 20 MLP SAE latents, measure their effects on Layer 21 residual SAE latents, and compare effect-vector cosine similarity for pairs that do not co-activate.

conditions.value: SAE B latents on the final token; effects summed across prompts

rows.measure: Whether cosine similarity of downstream ablation-effect vectors distinguishes non-co-occurring latent pairs judged to resemble feature absorption.
rows.value: The histogram was not bimodal; the metric was not strongly correlated with subjective judgments of feature absorption, and examples could be found at both ends of the distribution.
rows.note: Qualitative report of the proposed detector's performance; the post gives no numerical correlation or histogram values. The co-occurrence data is described as based on ~1e6 prompts.
rows.check: This row reports the study's own detector performing poorly, not an effect named by any version. 'Absent' describes the detector failing, not a claim effect. It should be treated as a method-performance result.
